row.정의: 중력파 천문학의 8개 엔드투엔드 과제(Waveform, Remnant, Dynamics, Ringdown, Validity, Analytic, Template Bank, New Physics)로 코딩 에이전트의 과학 모델링을 평가하는 벤치마크. 에이전트가 만든 산출물(대리모델, 회귀모델, 해석적 수식, 템플릿 뱅크, 물리 구현)을 에이전트 작업공간 밖의 별도 평가기가 전체 검증 세트에서 과제별 고정 지표(파형 mismatch, 상대·정규화 오차, 템플릿 뱅크 상대 효율)로 채점한다. 제출물 무결성, 결과 점수, 작업 기록 진단의 3단계로 검증한다. 논문은 15개 에이전트 구성을 시도해 2개가 무결성 검사에서 탈락하고 13개를 채점했다. 예: Waveform은 학습 250개·검증 200개 시뮬레이션, Validity는 학습 393개·검증 393개 샘플.
row.대표 예시·설명: 에이전트가 과제별 프롬프트를 읽고 데이터를 확인해 코드를 작성·실행하며 모델을 만든 뒤 완료 문자열을 출력한다. 이후 별도 평가기가 산출물을 채점한다(과제 설명).
row.이용 시 유의사항: 라이선스·상업적 이용·수정·재배포·lm-eval 지원 여부는 아직 확인하지 않았다. 코드 라이선스는 데이터 라이선스를 증명하지 않으므로 이용 전에 데이터 카드와 저장소를 확인해야 한다. 논문은 에이전트 구성 간 연산 자원이 통일되지 않아 비교가 compute-normalized가 아니라고 밝힌다. 평가에는 PyCBC, LALSuite 등 물리 계산 환경이 필요하다.

english_copy.definition: gwBenchmarks evaluates coding agents on eight end-to-end gravitational-wave modeling tasks: Waveform, Remnant, Dynamics, Ringdown, Validity, Analytic, Template Bank, and New Physics. An evaluator outside the agent's workspace scores each submitted artifact on the full validation set with fixed task metrics, such as waveform mismatch, relative or normalized error, and template-bank relative efficiency. Evaluation covers submission integrity, outcome, and diagnosis of work records. The paper attempted 15 agent configurations; 2 failed integrity checks and 13 were scored. For example, Waveform uses 250 training and 200 validation simulations, and Validity uses 393 training and 393 validation samples.
english_copy.task: Waveform (surrogate model over an 8D parameter space)
english_copy.example: Task description: the agent reads a task prompt, inspects the data, writes and runs code to build a model, and prints a completion string. A separate evaluator then scores the artifact.

screening.paper_title: gwBenchmarks: Stress-Testing LLM Agents on High-Precision Gravitational Wave Astronomy
screening.abstract: Modern gravitational wave astronomy relies on modeling tasks that often require months of graduate-level effort, including building fast waveform surrogates from expensive numerical relativity simulations, modeling orbital dynamics of black holes, fitting merger remnant properties and constructing template banks. These problems demand extreme precision to support detection and parameter inference, with state-of-the-art models achieving $\lesssim 10^{-4}$ relative error. We study whether state-of-the-art LLM coding agents can perform such end-to-end scientific modeling, where success requires constructing models with stringent accuracy criteria and reasoning about physical systems. We introduce gwBenchmarks, a suite of eight tasks grounded in gravitational wave analytic calculations and numerical simulations collectively representing over $10^8$ core-hours of compute. The tasks span interpolation, regression, and high-dimensional time-series modeling, requiring a combination of numerical methods, machine learning, and physics-informed approaches. In preliminary experiments, agents frequently relied on proxy metrics, partial evaluation, or fabricated results to spuriously complete tasks. We therefore implement an external pre-defined framework to gauge agent progress. Evaluating twelve coding agents, we find no consistent winner. On the easiest task, multiple agents converge to the same cubic spline solution, with one rediscovering a coordinate transformation widely used in the literature. On harder tasks like analytic waveform modeling, all agents fall 1-2 orders of magnitude short of domain requirements and exhibit systematic failures, including metric misuse, constraint violations, and result fabrication. Our code, data, and website are publicly available.
